_description: Service Bus resource schema for Version B (Logic Apps). Not an ARM template - a readable config manifest paired with the Azure CLI commands used to provision it. See 'provisioning.commands' for the exact commands, and 'provisioning.notes' for gotchas.

namespace.name: expense-approval-ns
namespace.reason: Standard tier is required for Topics/Subscriptions (Basic tier only supports Queues)

queues.name: incoming-expenses
queues.description: Landing zone for validated expense submissions. Consumed exactly once by the Logic App orchestrator using peek-lock.

topics.name: expense-outcomes
topics.description: Fan-out point for final expense decisions published by the Logic App. Each message carries a custom 'status' application property used for content-based routing to subscriptions.

subscriptions.name: approved-subscription
subscriptions.consumedBy: notify_approved (Azure Function, Service Bus topic trigger)

subscriptions.name: rejected-subscription
subscriptions.consumedBy: notify_rejected (Azure Function, Service Bus topic trigger)

subscriptions.name: escalated-subscription
subscriptions.consumedBy: notify_escalated (Azure Function, Service Bus topic trigger) - could also fan out an additional Teams/email alert to finance since escalation implies the manager missed the SLA

commands: az servicebus namespace create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --name expense-approval-ns --sku Standard

az servicebus queue create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --name incoming-expenses --max-delivery-count 5 --lock-duration PT5M --enable-dead-lettering-on-message-expiration true
az servicebus topic create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --name expense-outcomes
az servicebus topic subscription create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --name approved-subscription

az servicebus topic subscription rule create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --subscription-name approved-subscription --name approved-filter --filter-sql-expression "status = 'approved'"

az servicebus topic subscription rule delete --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --subscription-name approved-subscription --name '$Default'
az servicebus topic subscription create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --name rejected-subscription

az servicebus topic subscription rule create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --subscription-name rejected-subscription --name rejected-filter --filter-sql-expression "status = 'rejected'"

az servicebus topic subscription rule delete --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --subscription-name rejected-subscription --name '$Default'
az servicebus topic subscription create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --name escalated-subscription

az servicebus topic subscription rule create --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --subscription-name escalated-subscription --name escalated-filter --filter-sql-expression "status = 'escalated'"

az servicebus topic subscription rule delete --resource-group rg-expense-approval --namespace-name expense-approval-ns --topic-name expense-outcomes --subscription-name escalated-subscription --name '$Default'
notes: Every subscription is created with a default 'TrueFilter' rule named '$Default' that matches all messages - it must be deleted (or replaced) after adding the SQL filter rule, otherwise every subscription receives every message regardless of status.

The 'ServiceBusConnection' app setting (Function App and Logic App API connection) should use a namespace-level Shared Access Policy scoped to only the permissions each component needs (Send for the Function's queue output binding, Listen for the topic-trigered notification functions).
For production, replace the connection-string based auth with a managed identity + Azure RBAC (Azure Service Bus Data Sender / Data Receiver roles) to avoid storing secrets in app settings.
